newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Marine escapes murder indictment in border case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marine escapes murder indictment in border case.

text.p: A Texas grand jury Thursday decided against indicting a U.S. Marine who faced possible murder charges for shooting dead a teen-ager herding goats near the Mexican border in May, officials said.

"The decision is a no-bill," Presidio County District Attorney Albert Valadez told reporters outside a courtroom in Marfa, Texas, where a grand jury investigated the death of 18- year-old Esequiel Hernandez.
Marine Cpl. Clemente Banuelos shot dead Hernandez near the Texas border town of Redford on May 20 when he and three other Marines were on an anti-narcotics surveillance mission.

The Marines said Hernandez had fired on them and was about to do so again when Banuelos shot him, but the dead man's family said he was simply herding his goats and only carried an old .22 caliber rifle to scare off wild dogs.
Valadez said a conviction would have needed the support of at least nine of the 12 jurors. He did not say how many voted for a conviction, but said they sided with the Marines.
"They believed the Marines were telling the truth when they said Zeke (Hernandez) fired the first shot," he said. "The grand jury believed the Marines were following the rules of engagement."
